title: Auto-rollback policy options brainstorm (Console + Rollouts)
body:
Working doc / brainstorm. Not a spec. Goal: align on policy UX + semantics before we lock API/config schema.

Context
- We’re wiring rollouts (canary + A/B + staged model deploys) to SLO monitors and auto actions.
- Customers + SRE want: “don’t page me for regressions we can safely auto-mitigate” + audit trail.
- Main UX challenge: expose enough power w/o letting teams accidentally create flapping / unsafe configs.

Key UX principle (draft)
1) Safe defaults first: templates with known-good windows/thresholds.
2) Advanced overrides exist but behind “Advanced” + with guardrails + warnings.
3) Make action semantics explicit: Pause vs Rollback vs Shift-to-baseline.
4) Always explain “why”: show evaluated signals, windows, sample sizes, and debounce state.
5) Prevent oscillation: minimum holdoff + capped number of auto actions per rollout.

Definitions (we should standardize language in Console)
- “Auto mitigation”: umbrella for pause/rollback/shift-to-baseline.
- “Pause”: freeze rollout progression (do not advance steps), keep current traffic split (or optionally revert to last stable? TBD).
- “Rollback”: actively revert traffic to last known-good (LKG) step/version; for A/B = shift all traffic back to baseline.
- “Suppression window”: temporary disable auto actions for a given scope (rollout, service/route, region, tier) with justification.
- “Known incident override”: if incident state is active for scope, do not auto-rollback (or do not auto-rollback, only auto-pause). Needs decision.

Policy scope options
We probably need both, but UX should pick one primary.
A) Policy attached to “Service/Route” default, inherited by rollouts
- Pros: consistent behavior, easier SRE governance
- Cons: more friction for experimentation
B) Policy attached to “Rollout” (per rollout config)
- Pros: flexibility for model onboarding
- Cons: teams can set unsafe configs; hard to manage

Proposed: Service default + per-rollout override (with reason field if override is riskier than default)

Template ideas (what shows in policy editor)
1) "Recommended (pause then rollback)"
- On fast burn breach: auto-pause immediately
- If breach persists for slow window: auto-rollback
- Rationale: gives humans a short window to look, reduces false-positive full rollback

2) "Conservative (pause only)"
- Always pause; never rollback automatically
- Intended for early adoption + new services

3) "Aggressive (rollback on fast burn)" (maybe enterprise-only?)
- Direct rollback on confirmed fast burn
- Only for high SLO maturity + strong monitor coverage

4) "A/B safety rail (shift to baseline)"
- For experiments: if SLO breach on variant, shift traffic back to baseline, keep experiment record

Tier mapping (rough strawman)
- Self-serve Hosted: template 1 by default? maybe 2 until monitor coverage is solid
- Dedicated: template 1 default, allow 3 with approval
- Private: template 2 default (operators more conservative), allow 1 if customer opts in

Signals (eligible SLO monitors)
- p95 latency burn-rate (preferred) and/or p99 for tail regressions (runtime team says p99 is noisy under batching changes; prefer p95 for auto actions, show p99 for debugging)
- Error rate (5xx + gateway timeouts)
- Saturation / queue depth? (maybe informational for MVP; can be eligible later)

We need explicit UX copy:
- “Latency SLO: p95 over last 5m/30m”
- “Error SLO: availability/error rate over last 5m/30m”
- “Monitor freshness: last datapoint < N seconds ago”

Action decision toggles (policy-level)
- [ ] Auto-pause on breach
- [ ] Auto-rollback on breach
- (A/B) [ ] Shift to baseline on breach

But we should avoid a combinatorial explosion. Maybe choose one “primary action” and one “escalation action”.

Proposed policy model (UX)
- Primary response: Pause | Rollback | Shift to baseline
- Escalation: None | Rollback | Page/Notify only
- Confirm condition: fast window + slow window (default)

Evaluation windows + burn rate semantics
- Default: fast window 5m + slow window 30m (from #eng-sre thread)
- Debounce: require X consecutive evaluations (or time) before triggering
- Holdoff after action: no further auto action for N minutes

Guardrails (must be enforced server-side; surface warnings client-side)
- Min sample size: do not act if < N requests in fast window (per scope). Needs N by tier.
- Min traffic share: do not auto-rollback on variant if traffic split < X%? (prevents 1 req = rollback)
- Max auto actions: 1 rollback per rollout step? or cap per rollout (e.g., 2 total)
- No rollback during first M minutes after step change (warm-up) to avoid false positives due to cache warm
- Stale monitor behavior: fail-open (do nothing) vs fail-closed (pause) — strong opinion needed

Stale/missing monitor semantics options
Option 1: Fail-open (recommended for MVP)
- If monitor missing/stale: do not auto-act; emit “monitor missing/stale” event; notify channel
- Pros: avoids freezing rollouts due to telemetry issues
- Cons: loses safety rail when you might need it most

Option 2: Fail-closed to pause
- If monitor missing/stale: auto-pause rollout
- Pros: safer on paper
- Cons: can block deploys during telemetry incidents; high annoyance

Middle ground:
- For prod tiers (Dedicated/Private): fail-closed to PAUSE only (not rollback)
- For self-serve: fail-open + warn

Suppression windows UX
Needs to be very explicit and auditable.
- “Suppress auto mitigation” button in rollout UI (admin-only)
- Choose scope:
  - This rollout only
  - This service/route (all rollouts)
  - This region
  - This customer tier
- Duration:
  - 15m, 1h, 4h, 24h, custom
- Required: reason (freeform) + ticket link (Jira/Linear)
- Visible banner: “Auto mitigation suppressed until <time> by <actor> (reason…)”

“Do not rollback during known incident”
We need to define “known incident” signal source:
- Incident-bot state? (incident declared for service)
- Manual toggle in Console?
- PagerDuty incidents? (not sure we integrate)

UX idea:
- Policy checkbox: “Suppress rollback when incident active (allow pause)”
- Show incident badge in rollout header; link to incident channel

Audit + explainability (Console requirements)
- Every auto action event should have a “Why?” panel:
  - Action taken + timestamp
  - Scope (route/model version/region/tier)
  - Policy version + template name
  - Monitor IDs used
  - Fast/slow window status (burn rates + threshold)
  - Sample size + freshness
  - Debounce state (e.g., “confirmed after 3/3 evaluations”)
  - Suppression status (if suppressed)

Policy editor UX sketch (text)
Section: “Auto mitigation (SLO-based)” with:
- Toggle: Enabled/Disabled
- Template dropdown (Recommended / Conservative / A/B)
- Show “Default thresholds” in read-only with “Customize” expander
- Advanced:
  - windows
  - min sample
  - holdoff
  - action escalation
  - stale monitor behavior
- Inline warnings:
  - “This configuration may cause flapping (holdoff < 5m)”
  - “Rollback enabled but monitor freshness check disabled (not allowed)”

Per-rollout overrides
What people want:
- For risky model upgrade, be more conservative (pause-only)
- For small canary, more aggressive rollback

UX: in rollout creation flow
- “Use service default auto mitigation policy” (default)
- “Override for this rollout” (requires justification)

Should overrides be allowed to be *more aggressive* than service default?
- Suggest: only if user has elevated permission + audit reason (RBAC tie-in; see INT-8832)

RBAC notes (for later but affects UX)
- Roles:
  - Viewer: can see events
  - Operator: can restart rollout after pause; cannot suppress
  - Admin: can suppress/override policies; can trigger manual rollback

Open questions (need Eng + SRE alignment)
1) Pause semantics: pause and keep traffic split vs pause and revert traffic to baseline?
   - I suspect: pause keeps current split; but “pause due to breach” maybe should revert? Confusing.
2) For A/B tests: do we ever rollback “model version” vs just shift traffic split? Probably shift-to-baseline.
3) Monitor staleness: fail-open vs fail-closed-by-tier (see above).
4) Dual signal requirement: should we require BOTH latency and error to breach? Probably OR, but allow policy to choose.
5) Warm-up grace period: how long after a step change before acting? 2–3m? Needs data.
6) Label cardinality: policy UX wants per-customer-tier/per-region; can become large if users create too many combos.
7) Should templates be immutable? (so SRE can say “Recommended means X”)
8) How do we represent “last known-good”? Is it last completed stable step, or last step with SLO healthy for Y mins?

Strawman config (for schema discussion only)
(Embedding this here so we can sanity check what Console needs to collect.)

Example 1: Recommended (pause then rollback)
{
  "auto_mitigation": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "pause_then_rollback",
    "signals": ["latency_p95", "error_rate"],
    "fast_window": "5m",
    "slow_window": "30m",
    "burn_rate_threshold_fast": "14",
    "burn_rate_threshold_slow": "2",
    "min_requests_fast": "500",
    "monitor_freshness_max_age": "120s",
    "step_change_grace": "3m",
    "holdoff_after_action": "15m",
    "max_actions_per_rollout": "2",
    "stale_monitor_behavior": "no_action_emit_event"
  }
}

Example 2: Conservative (pause only)
{
  "auto_mitigation": {
    "enabled": true,
    "mode": "pause_only",
    "signals": ["latency_p95"],
    "fast_window": "5m",
    "slow_window": "30m",
    "burn_rate_threshold_fast": "10",
    "burn_rate_threshold_slow": "2",
    "min_requests_fast": "800",
    "holdoff_after_action": "30m"
  }
}

Notes: burn-rate numbers are placeholders; SRE to provide tier-specific defaults.

Next steps
- Kenji: mock policy editor section with template dropdown + advanced expander
- Sean/Aisha: propose defaults by tier + stance on stale monitor behavior
- Jada/Chloe: confirm controller state machine implications for pause semantics + step grace period
- Paula/Marissa: decide which templates ship in MVP (my vote: 2 templates max)

Changelog (light)
- 2026-02-07: Added stale monitor options + suppression UX notes
- 2026-02-12: Added template set + pause vs rollback semantics questions
- 2026-02-21: Added strawman config examples + guardrails list
